statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 21% because the Friday session closed with mean reversion intact: the 30,737.07 cash session low held from 17:00Z through the 20:00Z bell, cash NDX closed 30,807.93 up 1.00%, and VIX settled 15.33, down 6.47% and within 0.03 of its session low.
recommendation: Tail moves down one point to 21% and stays inside the watch band, so the mapped policy state remains WATCH and Tail sits below the block threshold. The escalation condition published for this hour was a decisive loss of the 30,737.07 cash session low into the close. It did not happen. That low, first set before 17:00Z, survived the entire final three hours of cash trading, and the index closed 30,807.93, which is 70.86 above it, 61.21 below the 30,869.14 opening print and 209.60 points, 0.68%, under the 31,017.53 session high. Volatility confirmed the same reading: VIX closed 15.33, down 1.06 points or 6.47%, only 0.03 above its 15.30 session low, and WTI closed 91.43, down 1.55%, after the G7 reserve announcement. A session that ends with the day's low intact, the index recovered off it and the volatility surface pressed to its own low is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score measures. Two counterweights keep the reading at 21% rather than lower. NVDA closed 233.95 after printing a new 233.60 session low, 1.65% beneath the 237.87 intraday record it set in the morning, so index leadership faded into a close the index itself won, and Friday's advance was reported as concentrated with roughly three quarters of constituents below their 50-day average. The CBOE ten-year index closed 5.28%, up four basis points and two below a 5.30% session high, at a level last seen in 2002, and it firmed on a day when October rate-hike pricing collapsed from about 64% to 16%. The danger window is the single hour from 20:00Z to 21:00Z, which carries the weekly settlement on thinning liquidity after the cash bell. From 21:00Z CME Nasdaq-100 futures halt until 22:00Z on Sunday 4 October, so the remaining 23 forecast slots are untradable and are published at the 20% watch floor as weekend gap exposure.
headline: Cash NDX closes 30,807.93, up 1.00%, with the session low intact through the bell and VIX down 6.47% to 15.33, easing Tail to 21% into the 21:00Z settlement
body:
Cash NDX closed 30,807.93 (+306.37, +1.00%) against a 30,869.14 open and a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range, on a quote timed 20:26:12Z after the 20:00Z bell. The defining fact of the session's end is that the 30,737.07 low never gave way. It was already set before 17:00Z and survived the whole final stretch of cash trading, so the close stands 70.86 above it. The index nevertheless finished 61.21 below its own opening print and 209.60 points, 0.68%, under the session high, so the day's last move was corrective rather than extending. NQ December futures are 31,086.50 (+326.00, +1.06%) on a 20:16:19Z quote, inside a 30,760.25-31,282.25 range from a 30,771.25 open on about 569.84k contracts, with a 31,084.75/31,085.25 bid/ask, firming into the 21:00Z weekly settlement while still 195.75 below their own session high.

The volatility and energy readings both point the same way as the held low. VIX closed 15.33 (-1.06, -6.47%) against a 16.39 previous close, a 16.15 open and a 15.30-16.24 range, so it finished within 0.03 of its session low rather than expanding into the weekend. WTI closed 91.43 (-1.44, -1.55%) on a 20:16:50Z quote inside an 88.11-93.51 range, extending its decline after the G7 agreed a coordinated 100 million-barrel crude and diesel release through the International Energy Agency over four months, with substantial diesel volumes inside the first twenty days. Both subtract from the stress environment instead of adding to it, and the falling crude price matters doubly because energy is the main channel through which the open Middle East file transmits into the Nasdaq-100.

The cross-sectional picture stayed divided, which is why the dominant mode remains mixed. SMH closed 630.60 (+12.79, +2.07%) against a 632.27 open and a 628.55-636.25 range. NVDA, in contrast, closed 233.95 (+1.34%) against a 230.86 previous close, a 236.05 open and a 233.60-237.87 range: it printed a fresh session low late and finished 1.65% below the 237.87 intraday record it set in the morning, when its intraday market capitalisation reached about $5.7 trillion. Leadership faded into a close the index won, and the day's advance was reported as concentrated, with roughly 75% of constituents trading below their 50-day moving average. The broader tape closed with the S&P 500 at 7,722.72 (+0.73%), the Dow at 51,176.96 (+0.49%) and the Nasdaq Composite at 27,190.86 (+1.19%).

The rate backdrop is the standing amplifier carried into the weekend. The CBOE ten-year yield index closed 5.28 (+0.04) against a 5.24 previous close, a 5.22 open and a 5.16-5.30 range, two basis points under a fresh session high at a level last seen in 2002. The latest Federal Reserve H.15 column, for 1 October, carries the two-year at 4.78%, the ten-year at 5.24% and the thirty-year at 5.61%. That the long end firmed on a day when the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported September nonfarm payrolls up only 29,000 against an 84,000-90,000 consensus, unemployment rising to 4.2% against 4.1% expected and average hourly earnings up 0.1% to $37.81, remains the session's clearest dislocation: bond traders cut October rate-hike odds from roughly 64% a week earlier to about 16% while yields still rose.

Tail therefore eases one point to 21% rather than holding 22%. The escalation condition published an hour ago was a decisive loss of the cash session low into the close, and the opposite occurred. Stress eases two points to 76 on the volatility and energy compression while staying in the high band, because Friday still realised a 0.91% cash range with the long end at 2002-area levels. Confidence holds at 89 on a complete verified closing evidence set covering cash, futures, volatility, energy, semiconductors, megacap leadership, the long end, the payrolls outcome, Fed pricing and the seven-day calendar. Geopolitics remains an open but non-accelerating file: the United States maintains a naval blockade with additional carrier strike groups deploying, unknown projectiles struck three ships in the Strait of Hormuz on 30 September, and post-midterm military action has been publicly threatened, yet crude fell into the halt. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and not used: its collection status is partial and its 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z collection timestamp is far outside the 90-minute freshness limit. Independent research covered that ground instead.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available, covering the 20:00Z hour on 1 October through the 19:00Z hour today. Tail ran from 20% to 27% across the window. It opened at 20% and held that watch floor for eleven consecutive hours, through the U.S. afternoon on 1 October and the whole Asian session, then stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency. It returned to 20% for the 10:00Z and 11:00Z hours, then climbed through the payrolls release to 24% at 12:00Z, 25% at 13:00Z and the window peak of 27% at 14:00Z. Those two hours, 13:00Z and 14:00Z, are the only ones in the window published in the block band, and both were published while NQ held within 0.10% of its session extreme with no meaningful pullback. Tail mapped back to 22% for the 15:00Z and 16:00Z hours once a 0.81% retracement was actually observed, lifted to 23% at 17:00Z on a downside-aligned configuration, and eased to 22% for the 18:00Z and 19:00Z hours as that configuration stalled and the session low held. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 74% and 79%, and confidence held at 88% or 89% in every hour. The dominant mode was mixed in 19 of the 24 hours, with trend-up recorded only for the 08:00Z and 09:00Z European-morning pair and the 12:00Z to 14:00Z post-payrolls advance.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 21% for the current 20:00Z hour, one point below the preceding hour, because the Friday session closed with mean reversion intact rather than breaking down: the 30,737.07 cash low held through the bell, the index closed 70.86 above it, and VIX finished within 0.03 of its own session low. That single hour is the published danger window, covering the 21:00Z weekly settlement on thinning liquidity after the cash close. No slot in this window is published in the block band, because the amplifier stack decayed through the afternoon instead of aligning. From 21:00Z the horizon changes character completely. Weekly settlement prints and CME Nasdaq-100 futures then halt until 22:00Z on Sunday 4 October, which falls outside this window, so every slot from 21:00Z Friday through 19:00Z Saturday is untradable. Those 23 slots are published at the 20% watch floor, expressing weekend gap exposure carried from the settled level rather than any assumed price structure, since a closed hour cannot produce the repeated extension or failed retracement that Tail measures. The named conditions carried through the halt are the long end at 5.28% near 2002-area levels, narrowing megacap leadership with NVDA closing 1.65% under its record, a concentrated advance with roughly three quarters of constituents below their 50-day average, and an unresolved US-Iran file offset by crude falling on the G7 reserve release. Stress decays from 76% to a 70% floor across the weekend as distance from Friday's realised volatility lengthens, and confidence decays from 89% to 73% purely on evidence age, crossing from the high band into solid in the Saturday afternoon slots. The published checkpoint for the reopen is whether it holds inside Friday's 30,760.25-31,282.25 futures range; only a gap beyond it would be evidence capable of lifting Tail. The next scheduled catalyst, ISM Services at 14:00Z on Monday 5 October, sits beyond this horizon.
